name: Engineered Equipment Co-Alaska
old_description: The company specializes in the design and manufacturing of power generation systems and automatic transfer switches for low and medium voltage applications.
about:
Engineered Equipment Company (EEC) was established in Anchorage, Alaska, in 1967 by Richard (Dick) W. Spils, an engineer with Standard Oil who saw a need for a local representative to serve industrial product manufacturers in the state. The company has maintained continuous operations in Alaska since its founding. In 1994, J. Mark Wilson acquired the business and expanded its reach, opening a branch office in Bothell, Washington, in 2016 to cover the broader Northwest region.

EEC operates as a manufacturer's representative and distributor of electrical products and process measurement and control equipment. Its product portfolio includes electrical equipment, valves, pumps, and instrumentation from manufacturers. The company takes a consultative approach, working with customers to solve complex technical applications across industrial and heavy commercial markets. With offices in Anchorage and Bothell, EEC serves Alaska, Washington, Oregon, and Idaho.

The company's customer base spans process plants and large-scale commercial installations in industries such as power generation, water and wastewater, oil and gas, food and beverage, chemical, pulp and paper, semiconductor, life sciences, higher education, health care, transportation, and infrastructure.

EEC distinguishes itself as the longest-operating manufacturer's representative of process control and electrical equipment in Alaska. The firm emphasizes a combination of responsiveness and demonstrated technical competence to earn customer trust.

name: Engineered Plastic Components
old_description: Leading North American supplier of engineered plastic components for automotive, appliances, medical, and consumer industries
about:
Engineered Plastic Components (EPC Manufacturing) is headquartered in Lebanon, Kentucky, and operates a network of 21 manufacturing facilities across the United States, Canada, and Mexico. The company serves as a Tier 1 supplier to automotive OEMs and provides precision-engineered plastic components for appliance, medical device, and consumer product markets.

The company runs injection molding presses ranging from 25 to 4,400 tons, enabling production of small precision parts up to large automotive components. Core processes include two-shot molding, overmolding, insert molding, gas assist, and in-mold decoration. Secondary operations encompass hot stamping, pad printing, heat transfer, silk screening, heat staking, and multiple welding technologies (sonic, spin, vibration, hot plate, ultrasonic, orbital). Facilities also offer painting (1K/2K/waterborne), powder coating, metal stamping, cleanroom manufacturing, leak testing, and full assembly and sub-assembly. The Lebanon, Kentucky plant spans 250,000 square feet and operates 24/7; the Bellevue, Ohio facility covers 192,000 square feet with 71 presses; other sites range from 52,500 to 150,000 square feet.

EPC supplies complex instrument panel assemblies, interior and exterior trim with Class-A finishes, and painted components to major automotive OEMs. For appliance manufacturers, it produces control panels, structural housings, and components with UV stability and heat resistance. Medical device customers receive FDA-compliant cleanroom-molded surgical instrument components and diagnostic equipment housings made from sterilizable materials. Consumer product lines include electronics housings, protective cases, and appliance parts with emphasis on durability and aesthetics.

The company emphasizes its North American footprint, IATF 16949 and ISO 13485 certifications, and in-house metrology (CMM, vision, DSC) as differentiators. It also highlights environmentally conscious manufacturing using recycled materials and sustainable practices, along with a certified minority-owned facility in Osceola, Wisconsin that provides engineering, tooling support, and mold repair.

name: Ennis Fine Furniture- Boise
old_description: Celebrating 80 Years — Ennis Fine Furniture, Family Owned Since 1946
about:
Ennis Fine Furniture was founded in 1946 in Boise, Idaho, by Cecil Ennis and his brother-in-law after they returned from World War II. The pair purchased a former horse stable at 23rd Street and Fairview Avenue, remodeled it, and began selling furniture and appliances. The business remains family-owned, now led by the founder's grandchildren Rick, Jeff, and Cathy.

The company operates two showrooms — one in Boise at 275 S 23rd Street and another in Spokane, Washington — offering living room, bedroom, and dining room collections that include sofas, sectionals, beds, dressers, tables, and case goods. Ennis Fine Furniture positions itself as a destination for semi-custom and luxury furnishings, providing design consultation, custom finish selection, delivery, installation, and haul-away of old furniture.

The retailer serves homeowners throughout the Pacific Northwest, with customers citing purchases of dining sets, lighting, upholstery, and accessories. Testimonials highlight the firm's design assistance and personalized service, though no commercial or contract clients are mentioned in the available materials.

Ennis Fine Furniture emphasizes its multi-generational legacy and community roots as its differentiator, stating that clients become "part of our family" and that each purchase represents "a piece of history, a touch of artistry, and a home that tells your story."

old_description: Evans Food Company was founded in 1991 out of a passion for food and an entrepreneurial spirit.
about:
Evans Food Company was founded in 1991 in Springfield, Missouri, out of a passion for food and an entrepreneurial spirit. The company began as a manufacturer of food products for retail packaging and food service production, building a portfolio that now includes brands such as The Grove Salsa, Hopsing Gourmet Sauces, and Chill CBD Water.

The company operates as a co-packer and private label manufacturer, offering end-to-end services from recipe formulation and costing to label design, production, climate-controlled warehousing, and shipping. It handles both low- and high-volume orders across multiple packaging sizes for retail and food service channels, with a typical production lead time of two to three weeks after payment receipt.

Evans Food serves food entrepreneurs and established brands seeking co-packing or private labeling for sauces, dressings, salsas, condiments, soups, and side items. Customers range from startups developing their first product to companies expanding existing lines, such as a Hispanic-focused salsa and hot sauce brand that praised the firm’s persistence and competitive pricing.

The company emphasizes a blend of culinary expertise and business acumen, staffing chefs, logistics specialists, and marketing professionals to support brand development. A portion of proceeds from Chill CBD Water funds clean-water initiatives for Pygmy tribes in the Congo through the Fight for the Forgotten program.

name: EverGreen Treated Wood (DBA Iowa Wood Preservers)
old_description: We offer a diverse line of treatment products that allow us to treat and manufacture lumber products for various uses and applications.
about:
EverGreen Treated Wood, doing business as Iowa Wood Preservers, operates from its headquarters in Oskaloosa, Iowa, with additional facilities in Sutton, Nebraska, and Willmar, Minnesota. The company is family-owned and was founded by Vic Sowl, who remains listed as founder; his son Nick Sowl serves as president. The business began as a wholesale supplier of pressure-treated lumber and has expanded to three Midwestern locations serving regional markets.

The company pressure-treats and manufactures a range of lumber products for structural and specialty applications. Its treatment lines include CCA for commercial, industrial, and agricultural uses; MCA-based Lifewood Residential for exterior exposure; and Pyro-Guard fire-retardant lumber and plywood for enclosed structural applications. Value-added services include kiln drying after treatment (KDAT) to improve stability and allow immediate finishing, precision end trimming to uniform lengths, notched runner fabrication for shed foundations, and V-groove paneling for interior wall and ceiling use.

EverGreen serves agricultural, residential, government and utility, marine, and wood-foundation construction markets. Agricultural customers use treated posts and framing for barns, livestock buildings, and utility sheds. Residential buyers specify Lifewood for decks, framing, and guardrails. Government and utility projects call for fire-retardant and marine-grade plywood, while wood-foundation systems rely on pressure-treated lumber for below-grade durability.

The company states its focus is on delivering durable, cost-effective treated lumber across the Midwest, backed by a commitment to wood-preservation quality and customer service. UL listing is cited as a mark of compliance for its treated products.

name: Everlast Energy & Roofing
old_description: Everlast Energy & Roofing was founded in 2022 by stepbrothers Josh Jackson and Alex Ciccio with a simple but powerful mission: to bring honesty, reliability, and long-term value back to homeowners. Both born and raised in Connecticut, they saw families struggling with unreliable contractors, rising homeownership costs, and confusion around energy solutions.
about:
Everlast Energy & Roofing was founded in 2022 in Manchester, Connecticut, by stepbrothers Josh Jackson and Alex Ciccio. The pair returned to their home state with a mission to bring honesty and reliability to homeowners facing unreliable contractors and rising energy costs. What began in a small basement has grown into a local team of over 40 professionals.

The company provides a full suite of roofing and solar services for residential and commercial customers. Roofing work includes full tear-off replacements, repairs, commercial flat-roof systems (TPO, rubber), storm-damage restoration, inspections, and ventilation upgrades. Solar offerings cover custom residential and commercial installations, removal and reinstallation, repair and maintenance, battery storage, and EV charger installation. The team has completed more than 800 projects and serves over 1,200 homeowners across Connecticut.

Everlast serves Connecticut homeowners and businesses, with a focus on residential roofing and solar as well as commercial roofing systems. The company is the sole solar partner of the UConn Huskies and one of two vetted roofing providers for the university, a partnership it cites as validation of its quality. It also handles insurance-backed storm repairs for hail, wind, and nor’easter damage.

The founders started Everlast to give Connecticut families a company they could rely on for both roofing and solar, emphasizing transparent pricing, clear communication, and a 25-year transferable workmanship warranty on roof replacements. The company promotes a “one-day installation” model for solar and a five-step process designed to minimize disruption.
